The second pathway connects Sophoraflavanone A to Neuraminidase, which is targeted by Butyric Acid, and also to the rho-3 subunit. Both pathways involve the rho-3 subunit as a downstream target, suggesting a potential mechanism where Sophoraflavanone A modulates signaling through different receptors to influence the rho-3 subunit. The integration of these pathways highlights the rho-3 subunit as a shared target, possibly indicating a broader role in the downstream effects of these compounds. The evidence supports a mechanism where Sophoraflavanone A may exert its effects by modulating receptor activity, leading to the activation of the rho-3 subunit, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
